name: AgFunder
stage_focus: Seed, Series A
why_fit: AgFunder's oversubscribed $100M+ Fund IV backs seed-to-Series-A frontier agrifood technology including robotics and sensors, a category fit for a Raspberry Pi based environmental sensing platform for indoor mushroom and CEA growers.
notes: Fund IV targets frontier agrifood tech broadly rather than CEA specifically; confirm current sector interest before applying.

name: Anterra Capital
stage_focus: Seed, Series A (incubation onward)
typical_check_or_award: $1M to $10M initial check (stated on the fund's own site)
why_fit: Anterra's thesis is digital and data infrastructure across the agrifood value chain, and its newest fund explicitly targets vertical AI for agriculture, which matches the sensor node plus Cloudflare relay stack Crowe Sense represents.
notes: Stated initial checks of $1M to $10M are larger than a $150k to $250k raise; worth an intro but expect them to want the round sized up or to come in as a small add-on.

name: Fall Line Capital
stage_focus: Seed through growth
why_fit: Fall Line field-tests portfolio technologies like soil sensors and autonomous implements on the farmland it owns and manages, which maps onto validating a physical CO2, VOC and climate sensing node in real grow rooms ahead of a production run.
notes: Business model centers on row-crop farmland; confirm indoor/CEA fit rather than open-field ag before applying.

name: Astanor Ventures
stage_focus: Seed through growth
why_fit: Astanor explicitly funds controlled environment agriculture and impact-native agrifood startups from seed stage, making an indoor-growing environmental sensing platform a direct thesis match.
notes: Third-party trackers report an average seed round near $5M to $6M; confirm appetite for a $150k to $250k pre-seed check before applying.

name: iSelect Fund
stage_focus: Seed through Series A (some later follow-on)
geography: US (St. Louis, MO; primarily North America)
why_fit: iSelect's stated mission of funding sensor-based farm management tools and its indoor-farming portfolio company Artemis show a current appetite for exactly the CO2, VOC and climate sensing hardware Crowe Sense builds for indoor cultivation.
notes: Typically co-invests alongside a lead rather than leading rounds; plan to pair the pitch with another investor.

name: Middleland Capital
stage_focus: Seed, Series A (site language now skews later)
why_fit: Middleland's portfolio already includes precision-ag sensing hardware (EarthOptics maps soil data the way Crowe Sense maps grow-room air), showing the fund is comfortable underwriting physical agricultural sensing plays.
notes: Own site now describes backing companies with early revenues and de-risked technology rather than pre-seed; active via an Oct 2025 SEC Form D filing; verify appetite for a pre-revenue company before applying.

name: Acre Venture Partners
stage_focus: Seed through Series B
why_fit: Acre's current $140M Fund III already holds an indoor-farming software company (Source) and ag-robotics hardware bets, so a hardware plus software sensing platform for indoor mushroom growers sits inside their existing thesis.
notes: Third-party trackers report average seed rounds near $5M to $6M; confirm they will consider a smaller pre-seed check.

name: Radicle Growth
stage_focus: Early-stage seed, challenge and accelerator model
why_fit: Radicle's Digital Ag vertical and challenge-based sourcing model (its Sept 2025 AgRogue Growth Partners platform with Land O'Lakes) are built to surface sensor-and-data farm technology like Crowe Sense.
notes: Operates more as a challenge/accelerator platform than a direct-check VC; expect a program or industry-partner track alongside any capital.

name: SVG Ventures THRIVE
stage_focus: Early-stage accelerator plus seed investment
typical_check_or_award: Up to $1M for Global Impact Challenge finalists (stated by the fund)
why_fit: THRIVE's recent portfolio includes storage-monitoring sensor company Cellar Insights (Jan 2026) and its Global Impact Challenge funds early-stage agrifood hardware and software, both lining up with a pre-revenue CEA sensing node seeking pilot capital.
notes: Structured partly as an accelerator/challenge platform; the $1M figure applies to challenge finalists, not a standard seed check.

name: Better Food Ventures
stage_focus: Seed, Series A
why_fit: Better Food Ventures backs seed-stage software-driven farm tools, so Crowe Sense should lead with the Cloudflare relay, apps and CLI as the core product to match their stated thesis.
notes: States it deliberately avoids hardware-intensive investments; deprioritize unless the pitch leads with software.

name: Lemnos
stage_focus: Pre-seed and seed, hardware and deep tech only
why_fit: Lemnos is a hardware-exclusive early-stage fund with a track record in agtech and IoT sensing hardware, a close match for a Raspberry Pi based environmental sensing node moving from firmware-complete into pilot manufacturing.
notes: Check size and formal geography mandate not publicly disclosed; latest confirmed investment (FORT Robotics) closed Aug 2025 per third-party trackers.

name: HAX (SOSV)
stage_focus: Pre-seed, hard tech and physical product only
typical_check_or_award: Up to $550,000 pre-seed; first check $250,000 ($150,000 cash plus $100,000 in-kind engineering and lab support) on an uncapped post-money SAFE (stated on the HAX FAQ)
geography: Global; flagship 35,000 sq ft facility in Newark, NJ, plus Shenzhen, Pune and Tokyo
why_fit: HAX is a pre-seed program built for hard-tech founders with in-house mechanical and electrical engineers, DFM and small-batch manufacturing support, directly addressing the enclosure, sensor integration and pilot production run Crowe Sense needs before scaling.
notes: Six-month residency, rolling admissions; confirmed active with an Aug 2026 portfolio raise (Princeton Critical Minerals, $16M).

name: Lowercarbon Capital
stage_focus: Pre-seed through growth, climate tech with a large hardware-heavy sub-portfolio
why_fit: Lowercarbon funds deep-tech climate hardware and has in-house scientific and engineering diligence capacity that could evaluate a CO2, VOC and differential-pressure sensing node as CEA climate infrastructure.
notes: Portfolio skews toward large energy and industrial hardware at bigger checks than a $150k to $250k raise; verify fit before applying.

name: Techstars Future of Food Powered by Ecolab
stage_focus: Early-stage accelerator (pre-seed/seed), agtech and food-system tech including hardware
typical_check_or_award: $220,000 (Techstars standard terms: $20,000 for 5% common plus $200,000 uncapped MFN SAFE)
geography: Minneapolis-St. Paul program, part of the Techstars global network
why_fit: This is the direct successor to Techstars Farm to Fork and is purpose-built for ag and food-system technology, a natural venue for Crowe Sense's sensing node for indoor cultivation and CEA growers.
notes: Name changed from Techstars Farm to Fork; check size rose from $120,000 to $220,000 starting the Fall 2025 batch; 2026 cohort applications opened March 2026, confirm the next window.

name: Y Combinator
stage_focus: Pre-seed/seed general accelerator; 2026 Requests for Startups name agriculture robotics and physical hardware
why_fit: YC's 2026 Requests for Startups name agriculture robots and physical hardware as priority categories, and its flat $500k check would fund a Crowe Sense pilot production run outright.
notes: Not hardware-exclusive and highly competitive; the pitch would need to lean on the hardware and agtech RFS categories.

name: Elemental Impact
stage_focus: First-of-a-kind and early commercial deployment funding across energy, industry, food and agriculture, water
geography: US nonprofit platform (Honolulu, NYC, DC, San Francisco)
why_fit: Elemental Impact funds food-and-agriculture climate hardware moving from prototype into real-world deployment, which lines up with Crowe Sense's move from unit-tested firmware into a validated pilot run for CEA growers.
notes: Renamed from Elemental Excelerator; skews toward first-of-a-kind commercial deployment with historically larger checks than pre-seed, so a $150k to $250k ask may be below their typical deal; verify fit.

name: Canyon Angels
stage_focus: Pre-seed/seed, accredited angel group
why_fit: A Phoenix angel group meeting on the Grand Canyon University campus is a realistic first stop for a local hardware founder with an existing regional audience who needs warm introductions more than a cold pitch.
notes: Apply via their site; verify current sector appetite for hardware; no check size published.

name: Desert Angels
stage_focus: Seed/early-stage, accredited angel network
why_fit: Arizona's oldest and top-ranked angel network (number one in the Southwest per the HALO Report) gives a Phoenix hardware startup access to the state's deepest bench of accredited investors and 12 sidecar funds.
notes: Tucson-based, not Phoenix; apply through their standard screening process.

name: Invest Southwest (Venture Madness)
stage_focus: Early-stage investor and founder matching conference and network
why_fit: Arizona's longest-running venture conference (since 1992) exists to put Arizona tech founders in front of the state's active accredited investors, which is the local-network leverage a Phoenix founder with a built-in audience should use.
notes: Not itself a fund; an event and membership network, apply to pitch or attend.

name: Tallwave Capital
stage_focus: Pre-seed, seed and post-seed VC fund
why_fit: Named Arizona's most active venture capital firm two years running, Tallwave Capital is a Phoenix-metro fund whose local reputation and network could open doors beyond its own check for a Phoenix hardware startup.
notes: Historically software and consumer-tech leaning; verify current appetite for a physical hardware product.

name: Arizona Technology Council
stage_focus: Ecosystem and network organization, not a direct funder
why_fit: The state's main tech trade association runs founder-investor events (Tech Talent Summit, Startup World Cup AZ) and accelerator partnerships (LaunchAZ, Venture Start) that a Phoenix-based founder with a YouTube following can convert into investor introductions.
notes: Not a check-writer; value is network access and event visibility.

name: Coplex
stage_focus: Corporate startup studio and venture builder
why_fit: A Phoenix venture studio with a track record of building 350+ companies offers a local hands-on operating and fundraising network, though its usual model is building ventures for corporate clients rather than investing in an outside founder's company.
notes: Studio/builder model, not a typical outside investor; verify whether they take on independent founders at all.

name: AZ TechCelerator
stage_focus: Tech and hardware business incubator (medical devices, IT, renewable energy)
why_fit: A 66,000 square foot Arizona incubator built for hardware-adjacent sectors is a plausible fit for a Phoenix-area company that needs affordable space and mentors to get through hardware validation and a pilot run.
notes: Incubator resource (space, mentors), not primarily a capital source; transitioning into a rebranded Spark Surprise hub in 2026, confirm current program status.

name: Arizona Tech Investors (ATI)
stage_focus: Seed and early-stage angel group
why_fit: Arizona's largest angel organization lists advanced manufacturing and sustainability among its target sectors and screens three companies at each of five member meetings a year, a direct route for a Phoenix hardware founder to reach 100+ accredited local angels.
notes: Not on the original list; low velocity (latest disclosed deal Feb 2025, about one new investment per year per Tracxn); meetings in Jan, Mar, May, Sep, Oct; third-party listings cite $250k to $1M ranges but the group's own site publishes no check size.

name: USDA SBIR/STTR Phase I (NIFA)
stage_focus: Pre-revenue feasibility R&D (Phase I); Phase II funds prototype scale-up
typical_check_or_award: $175,000 max for most topics ($125,000 for topics 8.6 and 8.12); ceiling, not guaranteed
why_fit: Funds exactly the CO2, VOC and climate sensor hardware and firmware R&D Crowe Sense needs to validate for indoor mushroom and CEA cultivation.
notes: Historical ceiling was $100k, raised under SBA award-guideline increases; Phase I runs about 8 months; majority US-owned small business required; verify current fiscal-year topics and deadline.

name: NSF SBIR Phase I (America's Seed Fund)
stage_focus: Pre-revenue proof-of-concept R&D (Phase I); Phase II funds full prototype
why_fit: NSF explicitly funds small-business deep-tech hardware R&D, and a multi-sensor Pi-based environmental node with a Cloudflare relay is that kind of hardware and software integration project.
notes: 6 to 18 month project period; no cost share; recurring deadlines Nov 4 2026, Mar 4 2027, Jul 7 2027; Phase II follow-on available.

name: Western SARE Farmer/Rancher Grant
stage_focus: Producer-led on-site research and outreach pilot with a technical advisor
geography: Western region (13 states plus Pacific territories, including Arizona)
why_fit: A producer plus technical advisor structure fits piloting Crowe Sense sensor validation on a real Arizona mushroom or CEA grow without positioning the applicant as an operating farm.
notes: 2027 cycle open, closes October 28 (noon MDT per earlier notes; the page gives the date only); never claim a working farm in the application.

name: USDA NIFA AFRI, Agriculture Systems and Technology
stage_focus: Applied agricultural engineering and technology research, typically institution-led or partnered
typical_check_or_award: verify: no per-track cap published; overall AFRI awards range widely, check the current NOFO
why_fit: Agriculture Systems and Technology is one of AFRI's six priority areas and explicitly covers precision-agriculture sensing and engineering, matching Crowe Sense's environmental sensing platform for CEA.
notes: FY2026 deadlines have passed; FY2027 NOFO not yet posted as of Aug 2026; for-profits are eligible but AFRI leans toward research-institution-led projects, so a university or extension partner strengthens an application.

name: Arizona Innovation Challenge (Arizona Commerce Authority)
stage_focus: Early-stage technology venture competition, pre-seed/seed, Arizona-only
typical_check_or_award: Minimum $50,000 non-dilutive per awardee, up to 10 awardees per cycle (ACA July 2025 release)
why_fit: A state-run non-dilutive competition whose eligible industries include hardware and advanced manufacturing is a strong fit for a pre-revenue Phoenix hardware company that wants runway toward a pilot run without giving up equity.
notes: Also counts as an Arizona program; cycles are themed (Fall 2025 was SaaS-focused) so confirm the current theme and window; some secondary sources cite $100,000 per finalist but the official release says minimum $50,000; awardees get three months with an ACA Entrepreneur-in-Residence.

name: Arizona Specialty Crop Block Grant Program (AZDA / USDA AMS)
stage_focus: Industry-benefit research, marketing or technology projects for specialty crop sectors
typical_check_or_award: verify: about $1.25M total Arizona allocation for FY2026 split across awardees, no per-project cap published
why_fit: Cultivated mushrooms are a USDA-recognized specialty crop, so a sensing project framed as a broad benefit to Arizona mushroom and CEA growers, not a single-company sale, can qualify.
notes: Funds cannot directly benefit a single commercial product or company, so apply through or alongside a grower association, nonprofit or research partner; FY2026 deadline (March 6, 2026) passed; FY2027 cycle not yet posted and may add cost share.
